body:
CHIEF DISPOSITION: BLOCKER, UPHELD. And I want to name the shape, because it is the mirror
image of everything else we fixed today rather than a new thing.

THE FINDING: ProviderCall.promptTemplateVersion None and Some("") are STRUCTURALLY UNEQUAL but
share renderProviderCall, so candidateSet and the full ClaimMeta fingerprint collide.
CriticFinding.note has the same encoding. Two values the type says are different produce one
address.

Everything else today was a value claiming MORE than it knew -- an imputed 0.5, a fabricated
LinguisticallyEntailed, a ratio stored past 1. This is an identity claiming LESS than it must:
a function whose entire job is to distinguish, failing to distinguish. A content address that
cannot separate two distinct inputs is not a weak address, it is not an address. And the
failure mode is the worst available: a change from one value to the other is INVISIBLE to the
fingerprint, so a regression across that boundary can never be detected by the mechanism built
to detect regressions.

HOW TO FIX IT, and the choice matters more than the fix:

  (a) CANONICALIZE OR REFUSE AT CONSTRUCTION -- if Some("") is meaningless, do not let it
      exist. Normalize it to None, or reject it, so structural equality and the fingerprint
      CANNOT disagree because the ambiguous state is unconstructible.

  (b) MAKE THE ENCODING INJECTIVE -- render None and Some("") differently, so the fingerprint
      preserves a distinction the type can express.

TAKE (a) UNLESS YOU CAN SHOW Some("") MEANS SOMETHING. When equality and fingerprint disagree,
fix the side that ADMITS A MEANINGLESS STATE, not the side that reports it. Choosing (b)
preserves a distinction the domain may not have and leaves the type able to express something
that means nothing -- and every consumer then has to decide, forever, whether an empty template
version differs from an absent one. An empty prompt-template version is not a version. That is
the same smart-constructor move as InterviewSource, LatePoolingRecipe and PromptPackageManifest,
arriving in the provenance layer.

If Some("") DOES carry meaning somewhere -- a provider that genuinely reports an empty version
string distinct from reporting none -- then (b), and say where, because that fact belongs in
the type's documentation more than in the encoder.

EVIDENCE I WANT WITH THE REPAIRED SHA: a test that constructs both values and asserts their
fingerprints DIFFER (under b) or that the ambiguous one is unconstructible (under a). Not a
test that the current pair happens to encode distinctly -- a test that the property holds. And
check CriticFinding.note in the same pass rather than as a follow-up; collab named it and one
of these found by inspection usually means a third exists in a file nobody has read yet.

collab: this is the third real blocker you have found on this candidate after two rounds of
review that had already accepted it -- B5, B6, and now this. Every one was the kind that a
green suite would not have caught. Keep going.

new-engineer: this is not a criticism of the compiler, which is doing the hard part correctly.
Fingerprint injectivity is the sort of thing that is invisible until someone specifically looks
for it, and someone specifically looked.
